title: Computer-use AI agents in 2026: what they mean for SaaS product demos
summary: New computer-use models can now drive a browser almost like a person. What that means for SaaS sales and onboarding teams, and where AI demo agents fit.
body_markdown:
Computer-use AI agents are models that see a screen and click, type and scroll in real software, and in October 2026 the leading models got good enough to drive a web app for most of a task on their own. For SaaS teams, the most direct use is the AI demo agent, such as Karumi: an agent that opens your real product and shows it to a buyer, live, while it talks.


Karumi is an AI demo agent: an autonomous agent that shows a buyer your real product live, by voice or chat, and answers questions as it goes.


## What happened to computer-use AI in October and November 2026?


Three model launches and one sales story moved the topic from research to go-to-market planning.


- **Claude Haiku 5.5 (7 October 2026).** Anthropic reported 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1, the main benchmark for agents that operate a computer, for its smallest and cheapest model ([OSWorld 2.1 leaderboard](https://llmbenchmark.ai/benchmarks/osworld-2-1) , checked November 2026).
- **GPT-6.1 Terra (late October 2026).** OpenAI launched Terra as "fast and capable computer use at scale". OpenAI says it completes tasks "over three times faster" than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, as of November 2026 ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-1-terra/) ).
- **Gemini 4 Carbon (28 October 2026).** Google reported 81.5% on OSWorld 2.1, close to Claude Opus 5.5 at 81.8%, the highest score on the board ([OSWorld 2.1 leaderboard](https://llmbenchmark.ai/benchmarks/osworld-2-1) , checked November 2026).
- **ElevenLabs' inbound SDR agent (4 November 2026).** Fortune reported that the voice AI company's own inbound SDR agent handled over 3,000 leads this year and qualified over 90% of them in 32 languages without a person stepping in. A human rep joins after the screening. If an agent can hold the first sales conversation, the next question is whether it can also show the product ([Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/04/waters-new-ai-tool-targets-one-of-the-pharmaceutical-industrys-most-tedious-tasks-2/) ).


## What is a computer-use agent, in plain words?


A computer-use agent is a model with a loop around it. It looks at the screen (a screenshot, the page structure or both), decides the next action, does it, and looks again. The action can be a click, a key press, a scroll or a form entry.


Three parts make it work:


1. **The model.** Claude, GPT or Gemini decides what to do next.
2. **The computer.** A cloud browser or virtual machine where the actions happen. Platforms such as Browserbase, Browser Use and Skyvern provide this layer for developers ([Mastra comparison of 9 computer-use platforms](https://mastra.ai/articles/best-computer-use-platforms-for-ai-agents) , checked November 2026).
3. **The task.** A goal, such as "fill in this invoice" or "show the buyer how reporting works".


## Can a computer-use model run a live product demo on its own?


Not yet, and the benchmarks show why. OSWorld scores are often "partial" scores, which give credit for a task done in part. On the same OSWorld 2.1 version, Claude Opus 5 scored 77.67% on partial credit but 44.33% on full task completion ([AI agent benchmarks explained](https://fleeceai.app/blog/ai-agent-benchmarks-2026-explained) , checked November 2026). In a demo, a half-finished flow is a failed moment in front of a buyer.


A product demo also asks for things a benchmark does not test:


- **Product knowledge.** The agent must know which screen proves which value, not only how to click a button.
- **A sales conversation.** It must listen, ask a qualifying question, handle an objection and know when to stop showing and start booking.
- **A safe environment.** It must not create, delete or send real records in a customer's account.
- **Logins that stay valid.** The demo account must be signed in every time, at any hour.
- **Speed.** A buyer waits seconds, not minutes. A plan-click-check loop that is fine for back-office work feels slow in a live call.
- **Handoff and records.** The conversation must reach the CRM and the right rep's calendar.


So a raw model is a strong engine, but a demo needs a product built around that engine. That is the job of an AI demo agent.


## What does this change for SaaS sales teams?


The demo stops being a scarce resource. Today, a buyer who asks to see the product fills a form and waits for a meeting. With an agent that can drive the real product, the demo can start when the buyer asks.


In practice, this changes four things:


1. **Speed to first demo.** An agent can start the demo on the website, in a chat or from a link in an outbound email. See[why SaaS companies are replacing demo request forms](https://karumi.ai/blog/why-saas-companies-are-replacing-demo-request-forms) .
2. **What SDRs do.** The ElevenLabs story shows the pattern. The agent qualifies, and humans take the conversations that are already serious. A demo agent adds the next step: it shows the product before the human call.
3. **Coverage.** Buyers in other time zones and languages get the same demo quality. Karumi runs in the buyer's language, set by the demo link.
4. **Data.** Every agent conversation is a record of what buyers asked and which screens they wanted to see. Karumi syncs sessions to HubSpot and Salesforce.


In our experience, buyers ask about pricing, integrations and security early, often before a rep would show them. An agent that can answer and then show the matching screen keeps the buyer in the product instead of in a follow-up email.


## What does it change for onboarding teams?


Onboarding has the same problem as sales: people learn by seeing, and there are not enough people to show them. A computer-use agent can walk a new user through the real product, step by step, and answer "where is that setting?" in the moment.


Fortune also reported that ElevenLabs uses a coaching agent so new sales hires can practise customer conversations and onboard faster ([Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/04/waters-new-ai-tool-targets-one-of-the-pharmaceutical-industrys-most-tedious-tasks-2/) ). The same idea works for customers. A demo agent that knows the product can show a new admin how to set up a workflow, live, instead of sending a help article. Karumi supports this use on its[onboarding](https://karumi.ai/onboarding) page.


## Where do AI demo agents fit next to computer-use models?


The market now has four layers. They are not rivals. Each solves a different part of the problem.


Option What it is Shows the real product Talks with the buyer Sales context (qualify, CRM, book) Who builds it


Computer-use model (Claude, GPT, Gemini) A model that operates a screen Yes, if you give it a browser Only if you build it No Your engineers


Browser infrastructure (Browserbase, Browser Use, Skyvern) Cloud browsers and tools for agents Yes, as infrastructure No No Your engineers


Interactive or captured demo tools A click-through tour or captured copy of the product A copy, not the live app Some add a chat or voice layer Partly Marketing team


AI demo agent (Karumi) An autonomous agent built for product demos Yes, the real product, live Yes, by voice or chat Yes: qualification, CRM sync, booking Ready to use


Each layer does something well. Raw models give engineers full control. Browser platforms solve hosting, sessions and logins at scale. Interactive demo tools are fast to publish and fully predictable, because every step is fixed. Consensus, for example, says its AI Demo Agent runs on the same demo data as its live demos and lets buyers click and explore ([Consensus](https://goconsensus.com/ai-agents) , checked November 2026).


An AI demo agent sits on top. It uses a capable model to drive the product, then adds what sales needs: product knowledge, the conversation, safe access, the handoff and the data. Karumi works on the real product, not a recording or a replica, and it can also join Google Meet, Zoom and Teams calls. Read more in[is a Karumi demo live or a recording](https://karumi.ai/blog/is-karumi-demo-live-or-recording) .


## How should you evaluate a demo agent built on computer use?


Use the new models as a reason to test, not as proof. Ask these questions in any trial:


1. **Does it show my real product or a copy?** Both are valid. Know which one you buy.
2. **What happens when my UI changes?** Ask how the agent notices a new screen and keeps working.
3. **How fast does it answer and act?** Time it in a live session, not in a sales deck.
4. **Can it say "I don't know"?** A wrong answer about pricing or security is worse than a handoff.
5. **What can it never do?** It should not save, delete or send anything in a real account during a demo.
6. **Where does the data go?** Check the CRM fields it writes and the calendar it books into.
7. **What security proof is there?** For Karumi, the Enterprise plan includes SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and GDPR, as listed on[pricing](https://karumi.ai/pricing) as of November 2026. Details are on the[security](https://karumi.ai/enterprise) page.


On cost: Karumi does not publish a list price. As of November 2026, its pricing page offers Growth and Enterprise plans, says every plan is scoped to the number of agents, demo volume, languages and integrations, and says most teams start with a pilot on one use case.


## FAQ


### What is a computer-use AI agent?


It is an AI model that operates software through the screen, as a person would. It looks at the page, decides an action such as a click or a key press, does it, and checks the result. Claude, GPT and Gemini all offer this ability in 2026.


### Which model is best at computer use in November 2026?


On OSWorld 2.1, Claude Opus 5.5 leads at 81.8%, with Gemini 4 Carbon at 81.5%, based on scores the labs reported themselves. OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra focuses on speed and lower cost for computer use. Vendor scores use different settings, so test on your own tasks.


### Can I build an AI demo agent on a computer-use model myself?


Yes, the models make it possible. The hard part is everything around the model: product knowledge, the voice or chat conversation, safe demo accounts, logins, speed, CRM sync and booking. Our[build vs buy guide](https://karumi.ai/blog/build-vs-buy-ai-demo-agent) lists the work in detail.


### How is an AI demo agent different from an AI SDR?


An AI SDR qualifies leads and books meetings, often by email or phone. An AI demo agent also shows the product, live, during the conversation. Many teams use both: the SDR agent finds the buyer, and the demo agent proves the value. See[what is an AI demo agent](https://karumi.ai/blog/what-is-an-ai-demo-agent) .


### Is a demo by a computer-use agent safe for my product?


It can be, if the agent works in a demo account and is blocked from actions that save, delete or send real data. Ask every vendor what the agent can never do, and where session data is stored.


### Does Karumi use computer-use technology?


Karumi is an autonomous agent that understands your product, decides what to show and drives the real product live in a browser while it talks with the buyer. It adapts to each buyer instead of following a fixed tour.
